title: Centralize Terraform blueprints, decouple env overlays, and migrate AWS provider to v5
creator: Asha Patel
description: Refactor our Terraform repo to centralize 'blueprint' modules, remove duplicated environment overlays, and migrate the AWS provider bindings from v3.x to v5.x. This reduces ongoing maintenance friction from repeated module copies per environment, enables consistent tagging and subnet lifecycles, and allows us to take advantage of provider performance improvements and new features in v5. The work includes automated state migration for a subset of workspaces, CI changes to run the new module tests, and documentation updates for platform teams that consume the modules.
acceptance_criteria: Core blueprint modules live in modules/blueprints with stable public inputs and no environment-specific logic
Per-environment overlays use the new module inputs and are reduced to thin wrappers (no duplicated resources)
Terraform plan/apply works in non-prod workspaces against the centralized modules without drift
AWS provider upgraded to v5.x in root and module provider blocks with no breaking changes for supported modules
Automated migration script moves at least 4 pilot workspaces to the centralized module state safely and logs changes
CI pipeline runs module unit tests and integration plans for a matrix of envs and provider versions
Docs and upgrade guide published for downstream teams and PR linked in the ticket
tasks: Audit existing environment overlays and catalog duplicated resources across accounts/projects
Design canonical blueprint module interfaces and input/output shapes (tags, network settings, iam refs)
Implement centralized modules under modules/blueprints and migrate one sample service overlay
Add provider aliasing and upgrade pins to aws provider v5 in root and modules
Create automated terraform state migration tooling for moving from per-env module state to centralized module state
Update CI to run 'terraform validate', 'terratest' (unit), and a dry-run matrix using provider v4 and v5
Run pilot migrations for staging and integration workspaces and collect metrics
Write docs: module README, migration guide, and rollback procedures
Coordinate with platform teams for rollout window and communication
migration_steps: 1) Freeze changes to target pilot workspaces for a 30-minute window
2) Take state backup and snapshot S3/Backend before migration
3) Run migration script to import resources into centralized module state
4) Validate plan output with team and run 'apply' in staging
5) Run smoke tests (network connectivity, IAM access, resource tags)
6) Monitor drift for 48 hours, then advance additional workspaces in waves
testing_plan: Unit tests: terratest suite for new blueprint modules (network, iam, tagging)
Integration: run full terraform plan against a forked non-prod account using provider v5
Canary: deploy one low-risk service overlay to staging and validate traffic and metrics
Backout: re-run state restore from snapshot and reapply previous workspace configuration
rollout_plan: Perform pilot in staging (wave 1), then integration accounts (wave 2), then a phased rollout to production workspaces. Each wave limited to 1-2 workspaces per weekday with a 48 hour monitoring window. Notify platform slack channel and on-call before each apply.
rollback_plan: If migration causes regressions, restore terraform state from S3 snapshot, revert PRs in infra repo, and re-run apply on the previous configuration. Pre-created IAM and network changes will be reverted by state restore. Follow escalation path to infra-oncall if automated rollback fails.
risk: Medium — provider v5 includes behavioral changes around IAM role assumption and S3 resource handling. State migration has moderate risk of resource address changes if interfaces are not perfectly matched. Mitigations include pilot migrations, state snapshots, and conservative interface shapes.
notes: We intentionally keep provider aliasing for backward compatibility during rollout. Platform teams must be informed of small input signature changes (tagging keys) and given a 2-week migration window. Expected win: reduce duplicate module PR churn by ~40% and simplify future provider upgrades.
customer_notes: No immediate customer-facing changes expected. This reduces maintenance and speeds future infra changes which indirectly improves reliability and deployment speed.
follow_up: Post-migration: identify remaining duplicated overlays for removal
Schedule retro to review migration runbook and CI improvements
Plan provider upgrade for third-party modules in next sprint
